# v0.5 fixture derivations (GATE A) — hand-derived, never generated by the code under test

Square fixtures use `rsiLen=2, fastLen=1, slowLen=2, areaLook=5, botCtx=2, botMaxW=2, topCtx=3, topMaxW=2,
botSep=topSep=5, turnMax=12, turnHold=2` (bar-count gates as the Pine defines them, small lengths so the series are
exact fractions). Tolerance 1e-5, values written to 6 decimals.

* RSI(2): `U_t = (u_t + U_{t-1})/2`, `D_t = (d_t + D_{t-1})/2`, seeded at t=2 with the mean of the changes at t=1,2;
  `RSI = D==0 ? 100 : U==0 ? 0 : 100·U/(U+D)`; na at t=0,1.
* `fast = RSI`, `slow = (RSI_t + RSI_{t-1})/2`; `isRed = fast > slow ⇔ RSI_t > RSI_{t-1}`; false while na (NA1/NA10).
  With non-zero changes and RSI not pinned at 0/100 the RSI direction equals the sign of the close change (proof in the
  v0.4 derivations); pinned bars here: t=2,3 (RSI 100, 100 ⇒ lime).
* Wedge detector at bar b: offsets 0..ctx−1 context colour, ctx..ctx+w−1 wedge colour, ctx+w..ctx+w+ctx−1 context colour,
  smallest w first. Area gate reads `inLow[ctx]` / `inHigh[ctx]`, i.e. the newest wedge bar. `posW` uses the window of
  areaLook slows INCLUDING the bar; 0.5 while the window holds na.
* Turn at bar b: armed, `fast>slow` on b−turnHold..b (rising RSI three bars in a row) and crossover at b−turnHold
  (RSI_{b−2} > RSI_{b−3} rule: rising at b−2 after falling-or-flat at b−3). Gap = (b−turnHold) − lastWedgeBar.
* Legs: path accumulates from the bar AFTER the opening turn up to and including the closing turn bar.

## ticks.csv (atrLen=2, wick gates at defaults) — same bars as the v0.4 tick fixture
`TR_0 = h−l`, `ATR_1 = (TR_0+TR_1)/2`, `ATR_t = (TR_t + ATR_{t−1})/2`. TOP tick fires at 4 (3.9/2.6125 = 1.492823) and 9
(7.6/5.106640625 = 1.488258); BOT tick at 5 (4/3.40625 = 1.174312). Blocks: ATR na → `atrV > 0` false (0); wick/range
(1); wick/ATR (2, 6, 7, 8); rng == 0 (3). Note: with rng > 0 the RMA gives ATR ≥ TR/len > 0, so `atrV > 0` can only fail
while ATR is na or every TR in history is zero (then rng is zero too); bar 0 is that case.
